name: architecture-tabs
purpose: The architecture band of a product page: a horizontal section title with one large button, over a row of up to five tabs whose active tab draws its named diagram the full width of the frame. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'architecture-tabs', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `button`, `frame-box`, `media-tabs` and `diagram`. The tabs advance on a timer that pauses under the pointer or keyboard focus and never runs under reduced motion; that state is owned by `media-tabs`.
useWhen: To plot several architectures of one product, or one request across the platform, one diagram at a time.
avoidWhen: For features shown by an illustration each → use `feature-tabs`.
related: media-tabs` — the timed tab row this section renders through.
diagram` — the named architecture diagram each tab draws.
bestPractices: Keep to five tabs with `position` `top` or `bottom`, three with `left` or `right`; tabs past the limit are not rendered.
Give every tab a `diagram` from the diagram library and a stable `value`.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the band, rendered by the horizontal section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty.

props.name: position
props.doc: Side of the diagram the tabs sit on: `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`; left and right hold up to three tabs.

props.name: tabs
props.doc: The architectures, in order; each is `{ value, title, description, diagram }` where `diagram` is the name of the diagram drawn while the tab is active.

props.name: primaryAction
props.doc: Large button in the section title; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import ArchitectureTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/architecture-tabs'

  const tabs = [
    {
      value: 'request-path',
      title: 'Request path',
      description:
        'A call crosses Firewall, the application and the function before it reaches a model.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway'
    },
    {
      value: 'failover',
      title: 'Provider failover',
      description: 'When a provider degrades, the gateway moves to the next model on the alias.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway-provider-failover'
    },
    {
      value: 'costs',
      title: 'Cost routing',
      description: 'Premium tokens go only where they pay off; everyone else gets a lighter model.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway-model-routing'
    },
    {
      value: 'latency',
      title: 'Latency routing',
      description: 'Real-time tasks run on AI Inference, close to the user, in under 30 ms.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway-latency-routing'
    },
    {
      value: 'cache',
      title: 'Response cache',
      description:
        'A repeated prompt is answered from cache, with no model call and no tokens spent.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway-response-cache'
    }
  ]

  const primaryAction = {
    label: 'Docs',
    href: '/product-preview',
    trailing: true
  }
</script>

<template>
  <ArchitectureTabs
    eyebrow="Routing"
    title="Every AI request through one control point"
    description="Every client calls one endpoint. Firewall stops abuse, then a function checks the key, routes the call, and logs it."
    position="bottom"
    :tabs="tabs"
    :primary-action="primaryAction"
  />
</template>
